subject: Re: Post-demo — Atlas Data trial scope, success gates, and integration plan
messages:
From: Alex Turner <alex.turner@atlasdata.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Singh <priya@atlasdata.io>
Date: 2028-05-10T14:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo — trial scope & integration asks

Irene / team, thanks again for the demo today — helped clarify a lot. We discussed running a 4-week trial against two production-like workflows (ingest + inference for enrichment, and a streaming request/response path for live triage).

Quick recap of what Atlas cares about for the evaluation: 
- Success criteria: 95th latency < 400ms for enrichment (batched), 99% availability during business hours, and inference output within expected fidelity thresholds vs. our golden set (we'll share).
- Integration constraints: we need a streaming endpoint for low-latency triage (websocket or HTTP/2) and programmatic function-calling support to attach structured metadata to responses.
- Security/compliance: SOC2 doc and a list of data residency options.

Next steps from our side: Priya will circulate the golden-set examples and the procurement windows (legal/PO). From Redwood side we'd ask for a short implementation plan with owners, SDK routes to use, and a rough timeline so we can align internal stakeholders.

Attachments: atlas_poc_requirements.pdf (our internal acceptance checklist)

Thanks,
Alex Turner
Director, Data Platforms — Atlas Data

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-demo — trial scope & integration asks

Alex — really appreciate the clear spec. Proposal below is our recommended POC runbook and the initial technical plan; I looped Dev and Marissa for implementation and success gating.

Summary (4-week trial, two parallel flows):
1) Enrichment flow (batch + nearline):
   - Objective: Verify cost per enriched record and 95th percentile latency under expected batch sizes (1k records / minute).
   - Success gates: 95th latency < 400ms; per-token unit cost within agreed threshold; no functional regressions vs. your golden set (comparison job).

2) Live triage (streaming, low-latency):
   - Objective: End-to-end median latency < 150ms; ability to do function-calling to attach structured metadata (severity, tags).
   - Success gates: 99% availability during 9am–6pm PT; function calls supported with payloads up to 2KB.

Implementation plan (owner tags and timeline):
- Week 0 (this week): Kickoff + environment access (Redwood test keys, VPC options if needed) — owner: Marissa Cole.
- Week 1: SDK integration and smoke tests (python/node sample apps, streaming route) — owner: Dev Patel.
- Week 2: Golden set runs and fidelity checks; cost telemetry enabled — owner: Irene Choi + Atlas data team.
- Week 3: Load and fault-injection tests, SLA validation; prepare acceptance report — owner: Dev Patel.
- Week 4: Final acceptance and optional follow-up items (quantization suggestions, routing rules) — owner: Marissa Cole.

Technical notes for the integration (Dev, can you confirm these routes and streaming options?):
- SDKs: python (redwood==2.x) and node (redwood-js). We will provide quickstart examples and a minimal sample app.
- REST route (batch): POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/enrich — payload: {records:[...]} — supports multipart/bulk semantics.
- Streaming route (low-latency): ws://stream.redwood.com/v1/triage or HTTP/2 /v1/generate-stream — prefer websocket for persistent context; supports per-connection KV cache for short-term context.
- Function calling: support via a structured "tools" parameter in request that returns structured metadata in the response envelope (JSON field: tool_calls).
- Telemetry: token-level cost, 95/99 latency buckets, and per-route error breakdown.

Attachments we'll provide: a skeleton SDK repo, an instrumentation checklist, and a short runbook for function-calling examples. I've attached a high-level integration_sketch.png to show the recommended topology.

Please confirm owners and the procurement timeline. If the plan looks good we'll lock dates and spin up test keys.

Best,
Irene Choi
Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
Phone: (415) 555-0192

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@atlasdata.io>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-13T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo — trial scope & integration asks

Irene / Alex — quick implementation details and a couple of options for streaming and function-calling. I've attached a small patch (redwood_sdk_patch.diff) with example snippets.

API and SDK specifics (confirmed):
- Batch enrichment (recommended):
  Endpoint: POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/enrich
  Headers: Authorization: Bearer <key>, Content-Type: application/json
  Body: {"records": [{"id":"...","text":"..."}], "route": "enrich-v1"}
  Response: {"results": [{"id":"...","prediction": { ... }, "tokens": 56, "latency_ms": 123 }]}

- Streaming triage (low-latency): two supported paths:
  1) Websocket (preferred for persistent context): ws://stream.redwood.com/v1/triage?api_key=<key>&conn_id=<id>
     - Messages: client sends incremental events, server streams partial tokens.
     - Per-connection KV cache: allowed with TTL up to 120s for triage use-case.
  2) HTTP/2 server-push /v1/generate-stream (alternate) — same semantics but without long-lived socket.

- Function-calling (structured outputs):
  Include parameter "tools": [{"name":"classify_severity","schema":{...}}] in request. SDK will surface responses as response.tool_calls where each call includes name, args, and confidence.

- Rate limiting and batching: we recommend continuous batching for the enrichment flow with batch sizes tuned to keep 95th percentile under 400ms. We'll provide target concurrency and batch window presets in the SDK quickstart.

- Telemetry endpoints: streaming logs will be visible in the Console; we will provision a temporary metrics dashboard and a GCP/Datadog webhook on request.

Attachments: redwood_sdk_patch.diff (contains PHP/py/js snippets and a streaming example), integration_sketch.png (topology).

Open questions I flagged for Atlas:
- Do you prefer websocket auth via query param (conn string) or signed challenge header (we can support both)?
- Are you planning to run the enrichment job from inside your VPC (we can push a VPC-resident agent) or from your public cloud environment?

I'll stand up a sample streaming app and push the quickstart repo by EOD Monday.

— Dev Patel
Sr. Software Engineer (Inference Integrations) — Redwood Inference

Thanks, team — that all looks good and addresses the items we discussed. A few notes and confirmations from Atlas: 

- Procurement: legal is OK to move quickly; PO expected by 2028-05-25. We'll need the SOC2 evidence and a short SOW to attach — Priya will handle with Procurement.
- Auth: we prefer signed challenge headers for sockets (better compliance posture).
- VPC: enrichment jobs will run inside Atlas-managed GCP project (we will want the option to pin a dedicated pool if possible).
- Golden set: Priya is uploading the test corpus today (you should see atlas_golden_set_v1.zip in the Drive link).

Acceptance checkpoints: once we have test keys we will run the golden set against the enrichment route and the streaming triage sample app. If gating metrics (latency & fidelity) pass we will sign acceptance and move to reserved capacity conversation.

Attachments: atlas_poc_requirements.pdf (updated with procurement timeline), SOC2_request_list.xlsx (will follow).

Alex Turner
Director, Data Platforms — Atlas Data
